bare_s1.explanation: The unit responds to two different things: car and truck wheels or rims, and framed rectangular panels on man-made objects such as screens, windows, wall pictures and slots in machines.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to two different things: car and truck wheels or rims, and framed rectangular panels on man-made objects such as screens, windows, wall pictures and slots in machines.
parsed.evidence: Seven of the 20 top boxes sit on car wheels, while most of the rest sit on rectangular inset elements: the computer screen, tablet, framed pictures, train and building windows, the remote's display, and the slots on the slot machine, toaster and payphone. Random photos with none of these still reach 1–4, so the unit is not very selective.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on wheels shown alone and on screens or windows away from vehicles, plus channel-ablation or feature-visualization data, would show whether a shared 'framed inset part' shape explains both groups.

Q0_s1.explanation: The unit responds to framed inset parts on man-made objects, where a bright or detailed interior sits inside a rim or bezel. Car and truck wheel rims are the most common case, extending to rectangular framed insets such as windows, screens, picture frames, display panels and slots.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to framed inset parts on man-made objects, where a bright or detailed interior sits inside a rim or bezel. Car and truck wheel rims are the most common case, extending to rectangular framed insets such as windows, screens, picture frames, display panels and slots.
parsed.evidence: 7 of the top 20 boxes land on car wheels (#5, 6, 12, 15, 16, 17, 20); most others land on framed rectangles: train and cab windows, a monitor, a tablet, wall pictures, a phone or remote display, a toaster slot and slot-machine buttons, all scoring 7-10. The random natural images (animals, food, plants) score only 1-4.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on isolated wheels versus isolated framed windows or screens, and on round non-wheel frames (portholes, clocks), would show whether this is one 'framed inset' feature or a wheel detector mixed with a window/screen detector.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds to small, sharply bordered inset regions: a framed, recessed panel whose interior is lighter or more detailed than the uniform surface around it. Its strongest responses are to rectangular insets, and it extends more weakly to circular rimmed insets with radial internal structure.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to small, sharply bordered inset regions: a framed, recessed panel whose interior is lighter or more detailed than the uniform surface around it. Its strongest responses are to rectangular insets, and it extends more weakly to circular rimmed insets with radial internal structure.
parsed.evidence: The top 20 activations (7-10) almost all mark a compact enclosed shape set into a surrounding surface: rectangular framed panels with contrasting interiors in the top 11, and circular rimmed shapes with spokes in many of the rest. The random sample, which lacks such framed insets, stays low (1-4).
parsed.missing_data: Activations on synthetic stimuli that separate rectangular from circular framed insets, and frame contrast from interior detail, would show whether this is one shape-agnostic 'bordered inset' feature or two separate ones.
